title: EnduraForge plan

profile.name: Salum
profile.experience: New to racing. Started running in October 2026; already swimming.
profile.diet: No breakfast. At most one smoothie a day, not every day. No whey protein. No testosterone-booster blends.

injury.note: A small pinch in the knee joint during the 8 km run in Dodoma on 14 Nov.

phases.name: Foundation: the 10 km
phases.purpose: Consistent running habits, run/walk efficiency, basic strength and swim endurance, ready for the 10 km.

phases.name: Endurance: the half marathon
phases.purpose: Long run grows step by step with easier weeks, aerobic base, muscular endurance and a longer non-stop swim.

phases.name: Ramadan: maintain and recover
phases.purpose: One light session a day around suhoor and iftar: keep the habit, keep strength, recover from the half marathon. No hard training while dry-fasting.

phases.name: Run and strength base
phases.purpose: Running and strength while the bike has not started yet.

phases.name: Triathlon development
phases.purpose: Cycling comes in after Ramadan: bike handling, cadence and easy endurance, first brick sessions, 1.5 km swims, strength still a priority.

phases.name: HYROX preparation
phases.purpose: Race-specific HYROX work: stations, running under fatigue, sled-style pushing and pulling, grip and wall-ball technique.

phases.name: Olympic triathlon tune-up
phases.purpose: Swim, bike and run together at Olympic distance, plus race nutrition practice.

phases.name: Ironman 70.3 preparation
phases.purpose: Long rides towards 90 km, long swims, long runs off the bike, race-day fuelling practice, then a two-week taper. Strength stays, at lower volume.

goals.achievable: 5.5 kg in 11 weeks is about 0.52 kg a week with a moderate deficit, three strength sessions and 160 g protein a day.
goals.relevant: Lighter = easier running and racing; better blood pressure and blood sugar.

goals.name: Keep it off and lean out further
goals.specific: After 09 Jan, keep a 7-day average under 83 kg and reach 77.0 kg by 22 Aug 2027.
goals.achievable: Small deficit (250 to 400 kcal) while training volume rises; never under-fuel long sessions.
goals.relevant: Power-to-weight for racing without hurting recovery or hormones.

goals.name: 10 km race in under 1 h 40
goals.specific: Finish the 10 km 10 km race on Sat 05 Dec 2026 in under 1 h 40 (100 minutes).
goals.measurable: Official or watch time. Type it in Your result.
goals.achievable: Needs 10.0 min per km with walk breaks. The long run builds gradually with easier weeks; progress shows your longest run against 10 km until race day.
goals.relevant: A key race on the way to the 70.3.

goals.name: Kilimanjaro half marathon in under 3 hours
goals.specific: Finish the 21.1 km Kilimanjaro half marathon on Sun 07 Feb 2027 in under 3 hours (180 minutes).
goals.measurable: Official or watch time. Type it in Your result.
goals.achievable: Needs 8.5 min per km with walk breaks. The long run builds gradually with easier weeks; progress shows your longest run against 21.1 km until race day.
goals.relevant: A key race on the way to the 70.3.

goals.name: Finish HYROX (Men Open)
goals.specific: Complete HYROX Men Open singles on 12 Jun 2027 in 1 h 55 or less.
goals.measurable: Official result, or your stopwatch for a full simulation at race weights.
goals.achievable: 7 weeks of station work, compromised runs and simulations on top of the run and triathlon base. First-timer finishes are commonly 1 h 30 to 2 h.
goals.relevant: Functional strength-endurance that also makes you a stronger triathlete.

goals.name: Finish the Olympic triathlon (tune-up)
goals.specific: Complete 1,500 m swim, 40 km bike and 10 km run on 11 Jul 2027 in 3 h 45 or less.
goals.achievable: A rehearsal of pacing, transitions and fuelling 6 weeks before the 70.3.
goals.relevant: Builds confidence and race skills for the 70.3.

goals.name: Finish the Ironman 70.3
goals.specific: Complete 1,900 m swim, 90 km bike and 21.1 km run on 22 Aug 2027 in 8 h 30 or less.
goals.achievable: Cycling from March, long rides building to about 3 h 15, long swims to 2.3 km and runs off the bike, then a two-week taper. 8 h 30 is the usual 70.3 cut-off.

goals.name: Swim 1,500 m non-stop
goals.specific: Swim 1,500 m of continuous freestyle without stopping by Sun 14 Mar 2027.
goals.measurable: Longest non-stop swim (m), logged after every endurance swim. Test swim on the day.
goals.achievable: Two evening swims a week, never on a run day. The Sunday non-stop swim grows about 100 to 150 m in normal weeks.
goals.relevant: The Olympic swim distance, reached early, so the 1.9 km 70.3 swim is the next step.

goals.name: Double my push-ups
goals.specific: Do at least 30 full push-ups in one set (or double your baseline if it is under 15) by 25 Apr 2027.
goals.measurable: Max push-ups test: chest to a fist from the floor, full lockout.
goals.achievable: Push-ups twice a week, from incline to feet-elevated, with tempo and load.
goals.relevant: Upper-body strength for HYROX, swimming and the physique you want.

goals.name: Strong hamstrings
goals.specific: Complete 3 x 5 controlled Nordic hamstring lowers (at least 3 s each, full range) by 25 Apr 2027.
goals.measurable: Reps with a 3-s lower, logged in the strength session.
goals.achievable: Hamstring work every week: walkouts, towel curls, then Nordics from February.
goals.relevant: Hamstrings protect you from the most common running injury and power the HYROX sled and lunges.

goals.name: Sleep 7.5 h
goals.specific: Average 7.5 h of sleep or more in at least 80% of weeks.
goals.achievable: Fixed wake time, lights out by 22:00, caffeine only before 12:00, phone outside the bedroom.
goals.relevant: Sleep drives fat loss, recovery, hormones and mood.

goals.name: Hit protein daily
goals.specific: Eat at least your daily protein target on at least 85% of logged days.
goals.achievable: Every meal in the meal plan is built on 40 to 60 g protein from local foods.
goals.relevant: Protects muscle while losing fat and speeds recovery.

goals.name: Ride 80 km non-stop
goals.specific: Ride 80 km in one go at easy endurance effort by 08 Aug 2027.
goals.measurable: Longest ride (km) from your logs or watch.
goals.achievable: Long rides grow about 15 min a week from mid-March, with easier weeks.
goals.relevant: The 70.3 bike is 90 km: 80 km in training means race day is within reach.

mini_goals.text: Baseline: longest non-stop swim (Sunday evening test)
Two weeks of lights out by 22:00 on 6 of 7 nights
Waist down 3 cm from baseline (enter waist in cm)
GOAL: 10 km race under 1 h 40 (enter minutes)
GOAL: Kilimanjaro half marathon under 3 hours (enter minutes)
Open-water swim 1,500 m with a buddy
Race-fuelling rehearsal: 60 g carbs an hour for a full long ride

baselines.label: Single-arm 20 L jerrycan row, weaker arm (reps)

library.name: Backpack goblet squat
library.setup: Feet shoulder-width, toes turned out slightly. Hug the loaded backpack high on your chest.
library.how: 1) Push the hips back and down between your heels. 2) Keep the chest up and knees tracking over the 2nd toe. 3) Go until the hip crease is below the knee. 4) Drive the floor away and stand tall, squeezing the glutes.
library.breathing: Breathe in at the top, hold it on the way down, breathe out as you pass halfway up.
library.mistakes: Heels lifting; knees caving in; back rounding at the bottom.
library.harder: Heavier backpack, or the pause squat.

library.name: Backpack pause squat
library.setup: Same as the goblet squat.
library.how: Squat down in 3 s, hold the bottom position for a full 3 s without relaxing, then drive up fast.
library.breathing: Hold the breath through the pause, exhale on the way up.
library.mistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom; relaxing in the pause.

library.name: Backpack Bulgarian split squat
library.setup: Stand about one big step in front of a chair or bed, rear foot laces-down on it, backpack hugged at the chest.
library.how: 1) Lower straight down until the back knee nearly touches the floor. 2) Front shin stays close to vertical. 3) Push through the front heel to stand. Finish all reps, then switch legs.
library.breathing: In on the way down, out on the way up.
library.mistakes: Front knee collapsing inward; leaning far forward; front heel lifting.
library.easier: No backpack, hands on a wall.

library.name: Jerrycan Romanian deadlift
library.setup: Feet hip-width, a jerrycan in each hand (or one held with both hands) in front of the thighs, knees soft.
library.how: 1) Push the hips back like closing a door with your bum. 2) Slide the jerrycan down the front of the legs to mid-shin, back flat. 3) Feel the hamstrings stretch. 4) Squeeze the glutes to stand.
library.breathing: In on the way down, out on the way up.
library.mistakes: Rounding the back; bending the knees into a squat; letting the jerrycan drift away from the legs.

library.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
library.setup: Stand on one leg, jerrycan in the opposite hand, knee soft.
library.how: Hinge forward on the standing leg while the free leg reaches straight back, until your body is nearly parallel to the floor. Hips stay square to the floor. Return by squeezing the standing glute.
library.breathing: In on the way down, out on the way up.
library.mistakes: Hips twisting open; rounding the back.
library.easier: Touch the back toe on the floor for balance.
library.harder: Heavier jerrycan, pause at the bottom.

library.name: Reverse lunge
library.setup: Stand tall, feet hip-width.
library.how: Step one foot back about 60 to 90 cm, lower until both knees are at about 90 degrees, back knee just above the floor. Push through the front heel to return. Alternate legs.
library.breathing: In on the way down, out on the way up.
library.mistakes: Front knee shooting past the toes; leaning forward.

library.name: Backpack reverse lunge
library.setup: Backpack on both shoulders, straps tight.
library.how: As the reverse lunge, with the load.

library.name: Backpack walking lunge
library.setup: Backpack on both shoulders, clear 10 m of floor or yard.
library.how: Step forward into a lunge, back knee lightly touches (or nearly touches) the floor, drive up and step straight into the next lunge with the other leg. This is the Hyrox sandbag-lunge pattern.
library.breathing: Steady breathing, one breath per step.
library.mistakes: Short choppy steps; torso falling forward.

library.name: Glute bridge
library.setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat, hip-width, heels 20 cm from the bum.
library.how: Press through the heels and lift the hips until knees, hips and shoulders are in a line. Squeeze the glutes 2 s at the top. Lower slowly.
library.mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of using glutes; pushing through the toes.

library.name: Single-leg glute bridge
library.setup: As the glute bridge, one leg straight in the air.
library.how: Lift the hips with the working leg only, keep the pelvis level.

library.name: Backpack hip thrust
library.setup: Upper back on the edge of a bed or sofa, backpack across the hips (hold it), feet flat.
library.how: Drive the hips up until the body is flat like a table, chin tucked, squeeze 2 s, lower under control.
library.mistakes: Overarching the back; feet too far away.

library.name: Calf raise on a step
library.setup: Balls of the feet on a step, door threshold or thick book, heels hanging off, hand on a wall.
library.how: Rise as high as possible, pause 1 s, lower slowly until the heels are below the step.

library.name: Single-leg calf raise
library.setup: As above on one foot.
library.how: Full range, 2 s up, 2 s down.

library.name: Wall sit
library.setup: Back flat on a wall, feet 60 cm out.
library.how: Slide down until the thighs are parallel to the floor, knees over ankles. Hold.
library.mistakes: Hips above the knees; hands pushing on the thighs.

library.name: Dead bug
library.setup: Lie on your back, arms straight up, knees bent at 90 degrees above the hips.
library.how: Press the lower back into the floor. Slowly lower the opposite arm and leg towards the floor, return, switch sides. The lower back never lifts.
library.breathing: Breathe out as the limbs lower.
library.mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor; moving fast.
library.harder: Hold a water bottle in each hand.

library.name: Front plank
library.setup: Forearms on the floor under the shoulders, legs straight, toes tucked.
library.how: Squeeze glutes and thighs, pull the ribs down, hold a straight line from head to heels.
library.harder: Lift one foot, or shoulder taps from a high plank.

library.name: Side plank
library.setup: Lie on one side, forearm under the shoulder, feet stacked.
library.how: Lift the hips so the body is straight. Hold, then switch sides (time is per side).

library.name: Bird dog
library.setup: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
library.how: Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until level. Hold 2 s, return, switch. Hips stay level (imagine a cup of chai on your back).

library.name: Hollow hold
library.setup: Lie on your back, arms overhead.
library.how: Press the lower back down, lift shoulders and legs a few cm off the floor into a banana shape. Hold.
library.easier: Knees bent, arms by the sides.

library.name: Incline push-up
library.setup: Hands slightly wider than shoulders on a bed, table or wall, body straight.
library.how: Lower the chest to the edge in 3 s, elbows at about 45 degrees from the body, press back up to straight arms.

library.name: Push-up
library.setup: Hands under the shoulders on the floor, body in a straight line.
library.how: Lower until the chest is a fist from the floor, elbows 45 degrees, press back to straight arms. Squeeze glutes the whole time.
library.mistakes: Head dropping; hips sagging; half reps.

library.name: Feet-elevated push-up
library.setup: Feet on a chair, hands on the floor.
library.how: As a push-up.

library.name: Backpack bent-over row
library.setup: Hold the backpack by the top handle or both straps, hinge forward to about 45 degrees, flat back, knees soft.
library.how: Pull the bag to your belly button, squeezing the shoulder blades together, lower in 2 s.
library.harder: Heavier bag, pause at the top.

library.name: Single-arm jerrycan row
library.setup: One hand and knee on a chair or bed, back flat, jerrycan in the other hand.
library.how: Pull the jerrycan up to the hip (elbow travels towards the back pocket), squeeze 1 s, lower until the arm is straight. This is your pull-up substitute.
library.mistakes: Twisting the torso; pulling to the chest.

library.name: Pike push-up
library.setup: Hands on the floor, hips high so the body makes an upside-down V.
library.how: Bend the elbows and lower the top of the head towards the floor between the hands, then press back up.

library.name: Backpack overhead press
library.setup: Stand tall, backpack held at chest level by the sides or straps.
library.how: Press it straight overhead, biceps by the ears, then lower to the chest. Ribs down, glutes tight.

library.name: Feet-elevated pike push-up
library.setup: Feet on a chair, hands on the floor, hips stacked high.
library.how: As the pike push-up.

library.name: Chair dip
library.setup: Hands on the edge of a sturdy chair behind you, fingers forward.
library.how: Lower until the upper arms are parallel to the floor, shoulders down away from the ears, press back up.
library.mistakes: Shoulders rolling forward; going too deep.

library.name: Jerrycan biceps curl
library.setup: Stand tall, jerrycan handle in one hand (or two smaller ones).
library.how: Curl up with the elbow pinned to your side, lower in 3 s.

library.name: Prone Y-T-W raise
library.muscles: Lower trapezius, rear shoulder, rotator cuff
library.setup: Lie face-down on the floor or a bed, forehead on a folded towel. Empty or small water bottles optional.
library.how: 1) Y: arms overhead in a Y, thumbs up; lift them a few cm, hold 2 s, lower. 2) T: arms straight out to the sides, thumbs up; lift, hold 2 s, lower. 3) W: elbows bent and tucked, hands by the shoulders; squeeze the shoulder blades back and down, hold 2 s.
library.mistakes: Shrugging; arching the lower back to lift higher.
library.purpose: Strengthens the muscles at the back of the shoulder that balance all the pulling in swimming.
library.cues: Shoulder blades down and back. Small lifts.

library.name: Backpack thruster
library.setup: Backpack held at the chest by the sides, feet shoulder-width.
library.how: Squat down, then drive up hard and use that momentum to press the bag overhead in one movement. Lower to the chest as you go into the next squat. This is the wall-ball pattern.
library.mistakes: Pressing with the arms only; half squats.

library.name: Burpee
library.setup: Stand with feet hip-width.
library.how: Squat, hands down, jump or step back to a plank, chest to the floor, push up, feet back in, stand and jump.

library.name: Burpee broad jump
library.setup: Clear floor or yard in front.
library.how: Do a burpee, then jump forward as far as you can, land softly, go straight into the next burpee.
library.mistakes: Over-reaching the jump and losing rhythm.

library.name: Farmer carry
library.setup: A full jerrycan in each hand, stand tall.
library.how: Walk with short quick steps, shoulders back and down, ribs down. Walk a loop of your compound or march in place if space is short.

library.name: Bear crawl
library.setup: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, knees hovering 2 cm off the floor.
library.how: Crawl forward moving the opposite hand and foot together, back flat. Turn and crawl back. Replaces the sled push.

library.name: Jerrycan swing
library.setup: Jerrycan held by the handle with both hands, feet wider than the hips.
library.how: Hinge and swing it back between the legs, then snap the hips forward so it floats to chest height. Arms are ropes; the hips do the work. Replaces the SkiErg.
library.breathing: Sharp breath out at the top.
library.mistakes: Squatting it up; lifting with the arms.

library.name: Squat thrust
library.setup: Stand tall.
library.how: Squat, hands down, jump the feet back to plank, jump them back in, stand.

library.name: Hamstring walkout
library.setup: Lie on your back in a bridge position, heels on the floor, hips lifted.
library.how: Keeping the hips up, walk the heels out in small steps until the legs are nearly straight, then walk them back in. That is 1 rep.

library.name: Nordic hamstring lower
library.muscles: Hamstrings (best exercise for preventing hamstring tears in runners)
library.setup: Kneel on a folded towel, heels hooked under a heavy bed or held by a partner.
library.how: Keep a straight line from knees to head and lower your body forward as slowly as you can. Catch yourself with your hands, then push back up to the start.
library.breathing: Breathe out slowly as you lower.
library.mistakes: Bending at the hips; dropping fast.

library.name: Backpack good morning
library.setup: Backpack on both shoulders, feet hip-width, knees soft.
library.how: Push the hips back and bow forward with a flat back until you feel the hamstrings stretch (about chest parallel to the floor), then squeeze the glutes to stand.
library.breathing: In on the way down, out on the way up.
library.mistakes: Rounding the back; bending the knees into a squat.

library.name: Water-bottle lateral raise
library.setup: Stand tall, a full 1.5 L water bottle in each hand at your sides.
library.how: Raise the arms out to the sides to shoulder height, elbows slightly bent, pinkies slightly up. Lower in 3 s.
library.mistakes: Swinging; shrugging the shoulders up to the ears.
library.harder: Fuller bottles or a 2-s pause at the top.

library.name: Jerrycan hammer curl
library.setup: Stand tall, jerrycan handle gripped with the thumb pointing up (or a bottle in each hand).
library.how: Curl up with the elbow pinned to your side and the palm facing in, lower in 3 s.

library.name: Diamond push-up
library.setup: Hands together under the chest, thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond.
library.how: Lower the chest to your hands with the elbows brushing the ribs, press back up to straight arms.
library.easier: On the knees, or hands on a bed.

library.name: Kegel glute bridge
library.setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat.
library.how: Lift the pelvic floor (as if stopping wind and urine), then lift the hips. Hold 3 s at the top, lower, and relax the pelvic floor fully.
library.mistakes: Holding the breath; clenching the buttocks instead of the pelvic floor.

library.name: Bridge march with kegel
library.setup: Hold a glute bridge.
library.how: Keep a gentle pelvic-floor lift and march: lift one foot a few cm, put it down, switch. Hips stay level.

library.name: Child pose belly breathing
library.setup: Kneel, sit back on your heels, arms forward, forehead down.
library.how: Breathe slowly into the belly and lower back. On each breath in, let the pelvic floor drop and relax.

library.name: Deep squat kegel pulses
library.setup: Sit in a deep squat, heels down (hold a door frame if needed).
library.how: Squeeze the pelvic floor for 5 s, then fully relax for 5 s.

library.name: Wall sit with kegel
library.setup: Back flat on a wall, thighs parallel to the floor.
library.how: Hold the wall sit with a gentle 50% pelvic-floor lift, then relax the floor before standing.

library.name: Diaphragm breathing
library.setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, one hand on the belly.
library.how: Breathe in through the nose: belly rises, pelvic floor relaxes. Breathe out slowly: pelvic floor lifts gently.

library.name: Dead bug with kegel
library.setup: Dead bug start position.
library.how: Lift the pelvic floor as the opposite arm and leg lower; release as they return.

library.name: Bird dog with kegel
library.setup: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
library.how: Lift the pelvic floor and reach the opposite arm and leg; hold 3 s; return and relax.

library.name: Happy baby breathing
library.setup: Lie on your back, knees to the armpits, hold the outside of your feet.
library.how: Rock gently and breathe slowly, letting the pelvic floor relax completely on each breath in.

library.name: Split-squat hold with kegel
library.setup: Split stance, lower into the bottom of a lunge.
library.how: Hold the bottom position: squeeze the pelvic floor 5 s, relax 5 s.

library.name: Side-lying clam with kegel
library.setup: Lie on your side, knees bent, feet together.
library.how: Lift the pelvic floor as you open the top knee, keeping the feet together; close and relax.

library.name: Elevator kegel in tall kneeling
library.setup: Kneel upright, hips over knees.
library.how: Lift the pelvic floor in 3 stages like a lift going up floors, holding 2 s at each. Lower stage by stage, then relax fully.

library.name: Bodyweight squat
library.setup: Feet shoulder-width, toes turned out slightly, arms forward for balance.
library.how: 1) Sit the hips back and down. 2) Knees follow the toes. 3) Go as low as you can with heels down and chest up. 4) Stand, squeezing the glutes.
library.breathing: In on the way down, out on the way up.
library.mistakes: Heels lifting; knees caving in; rounding the back.

library.name: Walking lunge
library.setup: Clear 10 m of floor or yard, hands on the hips.
library.how: Step forward, lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor, drive up and step straight into the next lunge with the other leg.
library.mistakes: Short choppy steps; front knee caving in.
library.easier: Lunge in place holding a wall.

library.name: Towel hamstring curl
library.setup: Lie on your back on a tiled floor, heels on a towel (or socks), knees bent, hips lifted in a bridge.
library.how: Keep the hips up and slide the heels away until the legs are nearly straight, then pull them back in with the hamstrings. That is the home version of the machine hamstring curl.
library.breathing: Out as you pull the heels in.
library.mistakes: Hips dropping; going too fast on the way out.
library.easier: Only slide out (lower the hips to come back).

library.name: Step-up
library.setup: A sturdy chair, bench or low wall about knee height that cannot slip (you have no stairs: test it first).
library.how: Place the whole foot on the step, drive through that heel to stand on top, control the way down. Finish all reps on one leg, then switch.
library.mistakes: Pushing off the back foot; knee caving in.

library.name: Water-bottle front raise
library.setup: Stand tall, a 1.5 L bottle in each hand in front of the thighs.
library.how: Raise the arms straight in front to shoulder height, thumbs up, then lower in 3 s.

library.name: Resistance-band row
library.setup: Loop a resistance band round a strong door handle or pole at chest height (band costs about 15,000 to 30,000 TZS).
library.how: Step back until the band is tight, pull the handles to your ribs squeezing the shoulder blades, return in 2 s.

library.name: Overhead triceps extension
library.setup: Stand or sit tall, a 1.5 L water bottle or the backpack held with both hands overhead.
library.how: Bend the elbows and lower the weight behind your head, elbows pointing up, then straighten the arms.
library.mistakes: Elbows flaring wide; arching the back.

library.name: Reverse crunch
library.setup: Lie on your back, hands by your sides, knees bent at 90 degrees above the hips.
library.how: Curl the hips off the floor towards the ribs, then lower slowly. Use the abs, not momentum.
library.mistakes: Swinging the legs; lifting the head.

library.name: Lying leg raise
library.setup: Lie on your back, hands under the hips, legs straight.
library.how: Lift the legs to vertical, lower them slowly until just above the floor without the lower back arching.

library.name: Mountain climber
library.setup: High plank, hands under the shoulders.
library.how: Drive one knee towards the chest, switch legs in a running rhythm. Hips stay level.
library.harder: Faster, or cross the knee to the opposite elbow.

library.name: Pallof press
library.setup: Band anchored at chest height to your side; stand side-on, hands at the chest holding the band.
library.how: Press the hands straight out, resist the band pulling you round for 2 s, bring them back. Do all reps, then face the other way.

library.name: Chair squat
library.setup: Stand in front of a sturdy chair, feet shoulder-width.
library.how: Sit back until you touch the chair lightly, then stand. Only go as deep as is pain-free; shins stay close to vertical.
library.breathing: In on the way down, out on the way up.
library.mistakes: Knees pushing far forward; dropping onto the chair.
library.harder: Lower seat, then the backpack goblet squat when pain-free.

library.name: Side-lying leg raise
library.muscles: Outer hip (glute medius): keeps the knee tracking straight
library.setup: Lie on your side, bottom knee bent, top leg straight and slightly behind you.
library.how: Lift the top leg about 40 cm with the toes pointing forward, hold 1 s, lower in 3 s.
library.mistakes: Rolling the hips back; toes turning up.

library.name: Straight-leg raise
library.setup: Lie on your back, one knee bent, the other leg straight.
library.how: Tighten the thigh of the straight leg, lift it to the height of the other knee, hold 2 s, lower slowly.
library.harder: 3 s hold, then a light ankle weight.

library.name: Slow kegel holds
library.setup: Lie on your back with your knees bent, breathing normally.
library.how: Squeeze and lift the pelvic floor for 5 s (8 s from the second week, 10 s later), then relax completely for 10 s.
library.breathing: Keep breathing; never hold your breath.
library.mistakes: Squeezing glutes or thighs; not relaxing fully.

library.name: Quick kegel squeezes
library.setup: Lie on your back with your knees bent.
library.how: One strong squeeze for 1 s, then 2 s of complete relaxation. Quality over speed.

library.name: Deep squat hold with kegel
library.setup: Sit in your deepest comfortable squat, holding a door frame if needed.
library.how: Hold the squat with a gentle half-strength pelvic floor squeeze, breathing normally; relax fully before standing.

library.name: Relaxation breathing
library.setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, one hand on your belly.
library.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose and let the belly and pelvic floor drop and widen; breathe out gently.

library.name: Streamline push and glide
library.setup: Stand in the shallow end with your back to the wall, one foot flat on the wall behind you.
library.how: 1) Arms straight overhead, one hand on top of the other, upper arms squeezing your ears. 2) Take a breath, sink under the water and push off gently with both feet together. 3) Face looks straight down at the floor, body long and tight like an arrow, toes pointed. 4) Glide without kicking until you slow down. Note how far you got. 5) Stand up, walk back and repeat. Try to glide further each time by being longer and tighter.
library.breathing: Breathe in before you push off; let bubbles out slowly through the nose while you glide.
library.mistakes: Lifting the head (the legs sink). Arms apart or bent. Pushing off with one foot or twisting the knee.
library.easier: Hold the pool edge with one hand first and practise lying flat face-down.
library.harder: Add 3 to 4 gentle flutter kicks at the end of the glide, then 3 strokes of freestyle.
library.purpose: Teaches the long, narrow body line every length starts with. A good glide saves energy on every wall.
library.cues: Squeeze the ears with the arms. Look at the floor, not forward. Tight belly and glutes.

library.name: Bubble breathing
library.setup: Stand in chest-deep water holding the edge.
library.how: 1) Breathe in through the mouth above the water. 2) Sink your face (or whole head) under the water. 3) Breathe out steadily through the nose and mouth: a long stream of bubbles, humming helps. 4) Come up only when the air is out, take a quick breath in and go down again. 5) Keep a calm rhythm: about 3 s out under water, 1 s in.
library.breathing: This drill is the breathing: out under water, in above it. Never hold your breath.
library.mistakes: Holding the breath and blowing it all out at the surface. Lifting the head high to breathe.
library.easier: Just the face in the water, holding the edge with both hands.
library.harder: Do it while kicking on your side, then while swimming freestyle.
library.purpose: Most beginners hold their breath under water, so they get breathless fast. This drill teaches you to breathe out fully under water so the breath in is quick and easy.
library.cues: Hum "mmmm" under water. Empty the lungs before you lift your head.

library.name: Kick on your side
library.muscles: Body rotation, balance, breathing position, kick
library.setup: Push off on your side: bottom arm stretched forward, top arm resting on your hip, one goggle in the water.
library.how: 1) Lie on your side with the bottom arm reaching forward and the top arm on your thigh. 2) Kick gently from the hips with long, relaxed legs and loose ankles (small, fast kicks). 3) Keep your face looking down at the floor; roll your head only to breathe, with one goggle still in the water. 4) Breathe out under water, roll the mouth up to breathe in, roll back down. 5) Swim one length on your right side, the next on your left side.
library.breathing: Out under water, roll the head with the body to breathe in. Keep the bottom ear on the arm.
library.mistakes: Bending the knees a lot (cycling kick). Lifting the head forward. Sinking hips.
library.easier: Use a kickboard under the front arm, or wear fins if the pool allows.
library.harder: Hold your side for 9 kicks, then take 3 strokes and roll onto the other side.
library.purpose: Freestyle is swum on your side, not flat. This drill teaches balance on your side and the head position for breathing.
library.cues: Hips high, shoulder of the top arm pointing at the ceiling. Kick from the hips, not the knees.

library.name: 6-3-6 drill
library.muscles: Rotation, timing, breathing to both sides
library.setup: Push off on your right side as in the side-kick drill.
library.how: 1) Kick 6 times on your right side, bottom arm forward. 2) Take 3 freestyle strokes, which rolls you onto your left side. 3) Kick 6 times on your left side. 4) Take 3 strokes back to the right side, and so on. 5) Breathe during the side kick, not during the strokes.
library.breathing: Breathe during the 6 kicks with one goggle in the water; breathe out during the strokes.
library.mistakes: Staying flat during the strokes. Rushing the 3 strokes. Lifting the head to breathe.
library.easier: 9 kicks instead of 6 to give yourself more time.
library.purpose: Joins the side position to the stroke and teaches you to rotate from hip to hip.
library.cues: Roll the whole body, not just the shoulders. Reach long with each stroke.

library.name: Catch-up freestyle
library.muscles: Long reach, timing, front of the stroke
library.setup: Push off in streamline, both arms out in front.
library.how: 1) Keep one arm stretched out in front at all times. 2) Pull with the other arm all the way back to the thigh, recover it over the water and place it on top of the front hand. 3) Only when the hands touch does the front arm start its pull. 4) Breathe to the side of the pulling arm, every 2 or 3 strokes. 5) Keep a steady flutter kick the whole way.
library.breathing: Breathe to the side of the arm that is pulling; one goggle stays in the water.
library.mistakes: Dropping the front arm while waiting. Crossing the hand over the middle line. Stopping the kick.
library.easier: Hold a kickboard in front and swap hands on it after each stroke.
library.harder: Three-quarter catch-up: start the pull when the recovering hand passes your head.
library.purpose: Stops short, rushed strokes. You learn to reach long and pull with one arm at a time.
library.cues: Touch hands in front, then go. Long reach, finish the push past the hip.

library.name: Single-arm freestyle
library.setup: Push off with one arm stretched forward (or resting by your side) and the other arm doing the work.
library.how: 1) Swim freestyle with the right arm only; the left arm stays out in front. 2) Rotate your body toward the pulling arm as it pulls. 3) Breathe to the side of the working arm, as it finishes the pull. 4) Swim 25 m with the right arm, then 25 m with the left arm.
library.breathing: Breathe to the working-arm side as the hand passes your hip.
library.mistakes: Pulling with a straight arm. Swinging the arm wide. Flat body.
library.easier: Do it with fins, or with the resting arm on a kickboard.
library.harder: Resting arm by your side instead of in front: much harder to balance.
library.purpose: Lets you focus on one arm at a time: the catch, the pull and the body roll that powers it.
library.cues: Elbow high, fingertips down at the start of the pull. Hips roll with the arm.

library.name: Fingertip drag
library.setup: Normal freestyle.
library.how: 1) As each arm comes forward over the water, bend the elbow and let the fingertips drag along the surface. 2) The elbow is the highest point of the arm; the hand passes close to your side and your ear. 3) Enter the water in front of your shoulder, not in front of your head. 4) Keep everything else as normal freestyle.
library.breathing: Normal breathing pattern, every 2 or 3 strokes.
library.mistakes: Swinging the arm wide and straight. Tense hand. Entering across the middle.
library.easier: Touch your armpit with your thumb on the way forward (zipper drill).
library.harder: Drag the fingertips more slowly while keeping the kick steady.
library.purpose: A high, relaxed elbow over the water protects the shoulder and keeps the stroke narrow.
library.cues: Elbow high, hand relaxed. Drag a line on the water from hip to head.

library.name: Fist drill
library.muscles: Forearm catch, feel for the water
library.setup: Normal freestyle with both hands in a loose fist.
library.how: 1) Make loose fists with both hands. 2) Swim freestyle: bend the elbow early so the forearm faces back and pushes water. 3) Swim 25 m with fists. 4) Swim the next 25 m with open hands and feel the extra grip.
library.mistakes: Pulling with a straight arm. Slipping and rushing the strokes.
library.easier: Alternate 4 strokes fists, 4 strokes open hands.
library.harder: Fists for a full 50 m, then compare stroke count with open hands.
library.purpose: With a closed fist you must pull with the forearm. When you open the hands again, the pull feels much stronger.
library.cues: Elbow high and in front, forearm vertical, push the water back to your feet.
library.dose: 4 x 25 m (alternate fists and open hands)

library.name: Sculling
library.muscles: Feel for the water, catch position
library.setup: Face-down in the water, arms straight out in front, a gentle kick (or a float between the legs).
library.how: 1) Point your fingertips slightly down, hands just below the surface, shoulder-width apart. 2) Sweep both hands outward a little, pitched outward like a windscreen wiper. 3) Sweep them back inward, pitched inward. 4) Keep the sweeps small and quick: you should move forward slowly. 5) Lift your head to breathe when needed, or roll to the side.
library.breathing: Breathe out under water; lift or roll to breathe in every 4 to 6 sweeps.
library.mistakes: Big wide sweeps. Bending the wrists. Sinking the elbows.
library.easier: Stand in chest-deep water and scull with the hands at hip level to feel the pressure.
library.harder: Scull with the hands under the shoulders (mid-scull) or by the hips.
library.purpose: Teaches the hand and forearm angle that holds the water at the start of the pull.
library.cues: Small figure-8 with the hands, wrists firm, elbows near the surface.

library.name: Bilateral breathing ladder
library.muscles: Breathing to both sides, even stroke
library.setup: Normal freestyle.
library.how: 1) First length: breathe every 3 strokes (left, right, left). 2) Second length: breathe every 5 strokes. 3) Third length: back to every 3. 4) Fourth length: every 2 strokes, as you would when tired in a race.
library.breathing: Breathe out steadily under water through the strokes so the breath in is short.
library.mistakes: Lifting the head forward to breathe. Shortening the stroke on the weak side.
library.easier: Every 3 for 25 m, then every 2 for 25 m.
library.purpose: Breathing to both sides keeps the stroke even and shares the work between both shoulders, which helps prevent shoulder pain.
library.cues: Same head roll on both sides; one goggle stays in the water.

library.name: Kick on your back
library.setup: Float on your back, arms by your sides, ears in the water, looking at the ceiling.
library.how: 1) Push off on your back, arms by your sides. 2) Kick from the hips with long legs; knees stay just under the surface. 3) Keep your hips and tummy high, chin slightly in. 4) Breathe normally all the way.
library.breathing: Breathe normally; the face is out of the water.
library.mistakes: Sitting in the water (hips sink). Big bent-knee kicks. Lifting the head to look at your feet.
library.easier: Hold a kickboard on your chest.
library.purpose: An easy way to train the kick without breathing problems, and it rests the shoulders.
library.cues: Toes just break the surface, little splash. Hips up.

library.name: Stroke-count lengths
library.setup: Normal freestyle at easy effort.
library.how: 1) Swim a length counting each hand entry. 2) Note the number (for example 22). 3) Swim the next length trying to take 1 or 2 fewer strokes at the same effort: reach further, glide a little. 4) Rest 20 s between lengths.
library.breathing: Your normal pattern; do not hold your breath to save strokes.
library.mistakes: Gliding so long that you lose speed and sink. Kicking harder to cheat.
library.harder: Keep the same count while swimming faster.
library.purpose: Fewer strokes per length at the same effort means a longer, more efficient stroke. Your watch shows this as SWOLF (strokes + seconds).
library.cues: Long reach, full push past the hip, push off the wall well.

library.name: Sighting drill
library.setup: Normal freestyle; pick a target at the end of the pool.
library.how: 1) Every 6 strokes, as your arm presses down at the front, lift the eyes just above the water (crocodile eyes). 2) Look forward at the target for a moment. 3) Turn the head to the side to breathe as normal; do not breathe forward. 4) Put the face back down and keep swimming.
library.breathing: Sight forward, then breathe to the side in the same stroke.
library.mistakes: Lifting the whole head and chest (the legs sink). Breathing forward.
library.harder: Sight every 4 strokes, at race pace.
library.purpose: In the sea there is no black line. You lift your eyes briefly to see where you are going without breaking the stroke.
library.cues: Only the eyes come up. Quick look, then back down. Press down with the front hand.

library.name: Freestyle (front crawl)
library.setup: Face-down, body long and flat near the surface, arms forward.
library.how: 1) Head: look at the floor just ahead; water line at the top of the head. 2) Entry: the hand enters in front of the shoulder, fingertips first, and reaches forward. 3) Catch: bend the elbow early so the forearm and hand face back. 4) Pull: push the water back past the hip with the whole forearm, rolling the hips with the stroke. 5) Recovery: elbow leads out of the water, relaxed hand swings forward close to the body. 6) Kick: small, steady kicks from the hips with relaxed ankles. 7) Breathing: roll the head with the body to the side, breathe in, roll back; breathe out under water.
library.breathing: Breathe out under water all the time; quick breath in at the side every 2 or 3 strokes.
library.mistakes: Lifting the head forward. Crossing the hands over the middle line (pinches the shoulder). Holding the breath. Big kicks.
library.easier: Stop at each wall; breathe every 2 strokes.
library.harder: Breathe every 3 strokes; tumble turns; swim at an even pace for longer.
library.purpose: The stroke for every main set and for triathlon.
library.cues: Long, relaxed, rotate. Hands in front of the shoulders, not across the middle.

library.name: Backstroke
library.setup: On your back, ears in the water, eyes up.
library.how: 1) Body long, hips near the surface. 2) One arm leaves the water thumb-first, straight, passing your ear. 3) It enters little-finger-first above the shoulder. 4) Bend the elbow under the water and push the water down to your thigh. 5) Roll the shoulders a little with each stroke; steady kick.
library.breathing: Breathe normally: in on one arm, out on the other.
library.mistakes: Sitting in the water. Head lifted. Arms entering behind the head.
library.easier: Kick on your back with a slow arm every few kicks.
library.purpose: An easy cool-down and a good balance to freestyle for the shoulders.
library.cues: Still head, hips up, long arms.

library.name: Brisk walk
library.setup: Flat path or the compound.
library.how: 1) Walk fast with a purpose, arms swinging. 2) Stand tall and land softly heel to toe.
library.purpose: Raises the heart rate and warms the muscles before stretching or running.
library.cues: Faster than a stroll, slower than a jog.

library.name: Leg swings front to back
library.setup: Stand side-on to a wall or tree, one hand on it.
library.how: 1) Swing the outside leg forward and back like a pendulum. 2) Start small and let the swing grow to a comfortable height. 3) Keep the standing knee soft and the body upright. 4) Swap legs.
library.purpose: Loosens the hips through the running range.
library.cues: Loose, controlled swing; the trunk stays still.

library.name: Leg swings side to side
library.setup: Face a wall, both hands on it.
library.how: 1) Swing one leg across the front of the body and out to the side. 2) Let the swing grow gradually. 3) Swap legs.
library.mistakes: Twisting the body with the leg.
library.purpose: Opens the hips sideways and wakes up the glutes that keep the knee in line.
library.cues: Hips face the wall; move from the hip.

library.name: Walking lunge with a twist
library.setup: Clear path of about 10 m.
library.how: 1) Step forward into a lunge; back knee lowers toward the ground. 2) Turn the chest toward the front leg, arms out. 3) Turn back to the middle and step through into the next lunge.
library.mistakes: Front knee caving in. Stepping too short.
library.easier: Smaller step; hold something for balance. During knee care keep the lunge shallow.
library.harder: Reach the arms overhead at the bottom.
library.purpose: Warms the legs through a big range and frees the upper back.
library.cues: Front knee over the middle of the foot; tall chest.

library.name: Ankle bounces
library.setup: Stand tall, feet hip-width.
library.how: 1) Bounce lightly on the balls of the feet, heels just off the ground. 2) Keep the knees almost straight and the contacts quick and quiet.
library.mistakes: Landing heavily on the heels. Bending the knees a lot.
library.purpose: Prepares the calves and Achilles for the impact of running.
library.cues: Quick, quiet, springy.

library.name: A-skips
library.setup: Flat 15 m.
library.how: 1) Skip forward: drive one knee up to hip height while the other foot taps down under the hip. 2) Swing the arms like running. 3) Keep the contacts light and quick.
library.mistakes: Leaning back. Landing in front of the body.
library.purpose: Teaches a quick foot strike under the hips, the action that reduces braking and knee load.
library.cues: Tall, knee up, foot down under you.

library.name: High knees
library.setup: Flat 15 m.
library.how: 1) Run slowly forward with fast, short steps, lifting the knees toward hip height. 2) Land on the balls of the feet; pump the arms.
library.purpose: Raises the heart rate and wakes up a quick running rhythm.
library.cues: Quick feet, tall body.

library.name: Butt kicks
library.setup: Flat 15 m.
library.how: 1) Jog slowly, flicking each heel up toward the buttock. 2) Keep the knees pointing down.
library.purpose: Warms the hamstrings and loosens the front of the thighs.
library.cues: Quick, light flicks.

library.name: Arm circles forward and back
library.setup: Stand tall, arms out to the sides.
library.how: 1) Make small circles forward, growing to big circles. 2) Repeat backward.
library.purpose: Warms the shoulder joint before swimming or upper-body work.
library.cues: Smooth, no pain.

library.name: Towel shoulder pass-through
library.setup: Hold a towel (or band) wide with straight arms in front of your hips.
library.how: 1) Lift the towel up over your head and down behind you, arms straight. 2) Bring it back the same way. 3) Move the hands closer only if there is no pain.
library.breathing: Breathe out as the arms go overhead.
library.mistakes: Bending the elbows; arching the back.
library.purpose: Opens the shoulders through the swimming range.
library.cues: Slow, ribs down, arms straight.

library.name: Doorway chest stretch
library.setup: Stand in a doorway (or next to a wall), forearm on the frame with the elbow at shoulder height.
library.how: 1) Step through with the same-side foot until you feel a stretch across the chest. 2) Hold, breathing slowly. 3) Swap sides.
library.breathing: Slow breaths; relax a little more on each breath out.
library.purpose: Undoes the hunched posture of desk work and the tight chest that pinches the shoulder in swimming.
library.cues: Gentle stretch, never pain in the shoulder.

library.name: Thoracic open book
library.setup: Lie on your side, knees bent to 90 degrees and stacked, arms straight out in front together.
library.how: 1) Keep the knees together on the floor. 2) Lift the top arm and open it across to the other side, following the hand with your eyes. 3) Pause, then close the book again. 4) Do all reps, then turn to the other side.
library.mistakes: Knees lifting. Forcing the arm to the floor.
library.purpose: A mobile upper back lets you rotate to breathe in swimming and stand tall when running.
library.cues: Knees stay down; move from the upper back.

library.name: Streamline reach
library.setup: Stand tall.
library.how: 1) Reach both arms overhead, one hand on top of the other, arms squeezing the ears. 2) Stretch tall through the fingertips for 5 s, then relax.
library.purpose: Rehearses the long streamline position before you get in the water.
library.cues: Ribs down, belly tight.

library.name: Cat-cow
library.setup: On all fours, hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
library.how: 1) Round the back up toward the ceiling, chin to chest. 2) Then let the belly drop and lift the chest and eyes. 3) Move slowly with the breath.
library.breathing: In as the belly drops, out as you round.
library.purpose: Moves the whole spine gently: good after sleep, sitting and long runs.
library.cues: Slow, full range, no pain.

library.name: World's greatest stretch
library.setup: Step into a long lunge, both hands on the floor inside the front foot.
library.how: 1) Drop the back knee if needed. 2) Lower the inside elbow toward the front foot. 3) Rotate and reach the same arm up to the ceiling, eyes following. 4) Return, then step to the other side.
library.harder: Straighten the front leg at the end for the hamstring.
library.purpose: One move that opens the hips, hamstrings and upper back before strength work.
library.cues: Long lunge, hips low.

library.name: Hip 90/90 switches
library.setup: Sit on the floor, both knees bent at 90 degrees and dropped to one side.
library.how: 1) Sit tall. 2) Lift both knees and rotate them to the other side. 3) Use your hands behind you for support if needed.
library.easier: Hands on the floor behind you.
library.purpose: Frees the hips in both directions of rotation.
library.cues: Tall chest, slow and controlled.

library.name: Hip 90/90 hold
library.setup: Sit in the 90/90 position.
library.how: 1) Sit tall over the front shin. 2) Lean the chest forward slightly until you feel the front hip. 3) Hold, then switch sides.
library.purpose: A longer hold of the 90/90 position to open the hips.
library.cues: Tall back.

library.name: Inchworm
library.setup: Stand tall.
library.how: 1) Bend down and put your hands on the floor (bend the knees if needed). 2) Walk the hands out to a push-up position. 3) Walk the feet in toward the hands. 4) Stand up and repeat.
library.breathing: Breathe out as you walk out.
library.purpose: Warms the hamstrings and shoulders together.
library.cues: Slow; tight belly in the plank.

library.name: Scapular push-up
library.setup: Push-up position (on the knees is fine), arms straight.
library.how: 1) Keep the arms straight the whole time. 2) Let the chest sink so the shoulder blades come together. 3) Push the floor away so the shoulder blades spread apart and the upper back rounds slightly.
library.purpose: Strengthens the muscles that hold the shoulder blade in place: key for healthy swimming shoulders.
library.cues: Arms straight; only the shoulder blades move.

library.name: First exercise, light
library.setup: Set up for the first exercise of the session.
library.how: 1) Do one set of 8 with about half the load (or bodyweight). 2) Focus on perfect form.
library.purpose: A light practice set grooves the movement before the real sets.
library.cues: Easy and smooth.

library.name: Child pose
library.setup: Kneel, big toes together, knees apart.
library.how: 1) Sit back on your heels. 2) Reach the arms forward and rest the forehead on the floor. 3) Breathe slowly into the belly and lower back.
library.easier: Pillow under the hips or forehead.
library.harder: Walk the hands to one side for the side of the back.
library.purpose: Relaxes the lower back and the pelvic floor.
library.cues: Let everything relax.

library.name: Child pose with side reach
library.setup: Child pose.
library.how: 1) Walk both hands over to the right; hold. 2) Walk them to the left; hold.
library.purpose: Stretches the big back muscles used in swimming.
library.cues: Hips stay back.

library.name: Lying hamstring stretch with a towel
library.setup: Lie on your back, towel around one foot.
library.how: 1) Straighten that leg up toward the ceiling until you feel the back of the thigh. 2) Keep the other leg flat on the floor. 3) Hold, then swap.
library.purpose: Keeps the hamstrings long without loading the back.
library.cues: Gentle stretch; knee almost straight.

library.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
library.setup: Kneel on one knee (cushion under it), other foot forward.
library.how: 1) Tuck the tailbone under and squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg. 2) Shift the hips forward until the front of the hip stretches. 3) Keep the ribs down. Reach the arm on the kneeling side overhead for more.
library.mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of stretching the hip.
library.purpose: Tight hip flexors from sitting pull on the pelvis and the knee. This is one of the most useful stretches for runners.
library.cues: Glute squeezed; small movement.

library.name: Standing quad stretch
library.setup: Stand tall next to a wall for balance.
library.how: 1) Bend one knee and hold the ankle behind you. 2) Bring the heel gently toward the buttock, knees together. 3) Tuck the hips slightly.
library.mistakes: Arching the back. Pulling hard on a sore knee.
library.easier: Lie on your side and hold the ankle; or use a towel.
library.purpose: Eases the front of the thigh, which pulls on the kneecap when tight.
library.cues: Knees together, hips forward.

library.name: Cross-body shoulder stretch
library.setup: Stand or sit tall.
library.how: 1) Bring one arm across the chest. 2) Hold it above the elbow with the other hand and pull gently.
library.purpose: Stretches the back of the shoulder after swimming.
library.cues: Shoulder stays down.

library.name: Overhead triceps stretch
library.setup: Stand tall.
library.how: 1) Reach one arm up and bend the elbow so the hand drops behind the head. 2) Gently push the elbow with the other hand.
library.purpose: Stretches the back of the arm and the side of the back.
library.cues: Ribs down.

library.name: Standing calf stretch on a wall
library.setup: Hands on a wall, one foot back.
library.how: 1) Back leg straight, heel down, lean into the wall: upper calf. 2) Then bend the back knee a little, heel still down: lower calf and Achilles. 3) Swap legs.
library.harder: Stand on a step and drop the heel.
library.purpose: Tight calves are linked to Achilles and shin pain in runners.
library.cues: Heel stays down; toes point forward.

library.name: Standing hamstring stretch
library.setup: Heel on a low step or kerb, leg straight.
library.how: 1) Keep the back flat and hinge forward from the hips. 2) Stop when you feel the back of the thigh.
library.mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the toes.
library.purpose: Stretches the back of the thigh after running.
library.cues: Flat back.

library.name: Figure-4 glute stretch, lying
library.setup: Lie on your back, knees bent.
library.how: 1) Cross one ankle over the opposite knee. 2) Pull that thigh toward your chest until the buttock stretches.
library.easier: Keep the foot on the floor.
library.purpose: Relaxes the glutes and outer hip, which affect the line of the knee.
library.cues: Head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.

library.name: Couch stretch
library.setup: Back knee on a cushion against a wall, shin up the wall, other foot forward.
library.how: 1) Lift the chest tall. 2) Squeeze the glute of the back leg. 3) Hold, then swap.
library.mistakes: Arching the back. Forcing it when the knee is sore.
library.easier: Knee further from the wall; hands on a chair. Skip during knee care if it pinches.
library.purpose: A deep stretch for the front of the hip and thigh.
library.cues: Tall chest, glute squeezed.

library.name: Pigeon stretch
library.setup: From all fours, bring one knee forward behind the same-side wrist, back leg long.
library.how: 1) Square the hips. 2) Fold forward over the front shin. 3) Hold, then swap.
library.mistakes: Twisting the front knee. If the knee complains, use the figure-4 stretch instead.
library.purpose: Opens the hip and glute.
library.cues: No pain in the knee.

library.name: Ankle rocks
library.setup: Kneel half-kneeling facing a wall, front foot 5 to 10 cm from it.
library.how: 1) Push the front knee forward to touch the wall, heel down. 2) Return and repeat. 3) Move the foot back as you improve.
library.purpose: Better ankle bend means less strain on the knee when running and squatting.
library.cues: Heel stays down; knee over the middle toes.

library.name: Deep squat hold
library.setup: Feet a bit wider than hips, toes turned out.
library.how: 1) Sit down into your deepest squat with the heels down. 2) Push the knees out with the elbows. 3) Hold a door frame if needed.
library.breathing: Slow breaths; let the pelvic floor relax.
library.mistakes: Forcing depth. During knee care sit only as deep as is pain-free.
library.purpose: Opens the hips and ankles.
library.cues: Heels down, chest up.

library.name: Legs up the wall
library.setup: Lie on your back with the buttocks near a wall.
library.how: 1) Rest the legs straight up the wall. 2) Arms relaxed; breathe slowly.
library.mistakes: Holding tension in the legs, neck or jaw.
library.purpose: Relaxes the legs and the nervous system on recovery days.
library.cues: Let everything go.

library.name: Sleeper stretch
library.setup: Lie on one side, lower arm out in front at 90 degrees, elbow bent so the hand points up.
library.how: 1) Use the top hand to press the lower forearm gently toward the floor. 2) Stop at a light stretch. Swap sides.
library.purpose: Gentle stretch for the back of the shoulder that tightens in swimmers.
library.cues: Very gentle.

library.name: Knees-to-chest rock
library.setup: Lie on your back.
library.how: 1) Hug both knees to the chest. 2) Rock gently side to side.
library.mistakes: Pulling hard on the knees or lifting the head.
library.purpose: Relaxes the lower back.
library.cues: Relaxed.

library.name: Supine spinal twist
library.setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, arms out.
library.how: 1) Drop both knees to one side. 2) Turn the head the other way. 3) Hold, then swap.
library.purpose: Releases the lower back after riding and long runs.
library.cues: Shoulders stay on the floor.

library.name: Outer-thigh roll on a full water bottle
library.setup: Lie on your side with a full, closed 1.5 L bottle under the outer thigh.
library.how: 1) Support yourself on your forearm and the top foot. 2) Roll slowly from just above the knee to just below the hip. 3) Pause on tender spots for a few breaths. Then do the front of the thigh.
library.breathing: Slow breaths; relax over the bottle.
library.mistakes: Rolling right over the knee joint.
library.easier: Less body weight on the bottle.
library.purpose: Eases tight tissue on the outside of the thigh that can pull on the outside of the knee.
library.cues: Tender is fine, sharp is not.

library.name: Side-lying external rotation
library.setup: Lie on your side, top elbow bent at 90 degrees and tucked to your side on a rolled towel, holding a 0.5 to 1.5 L water bottle.
library.how: 1) Keep the elbow on your side. 2) Rotate the forearm up toward the ceiling. 3) Lower slowly over 3 s. 4) Do all reps, then swap sides.
library.mistakes: Elbow lifting off the body. Rolling backward.
library.purpose: The rotator cuff keeps the shoulder joint centred. Swimmers who train it get far less shoulder pain.
library.cues: Elbow glued to the side; slow lowering.

library.name: Wall slide
library.setup: Stand with your back to a wall, feet a little forward, forearms on the wall in a goal-post shape.
library.how: 1) Keep the lower back, head and forearms near the wall. 2) Slide the arms up as far as you can without losing contact. 3) Slide back down, squeezing the shoulder blades down.
library.breathing: Breathe out as you slide up.
library.harder: Lift the hands off the wall at the top.
library.purpose: Trains the shoulder blades to move well overhead, the position of every swim stroke.
library.cues: Ribs down, slow.

warmups.title: Before every swim, on the pool deck (6 min)

mobility.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
mobility.how: Kneel on one knee, other foot forward. Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg and shift the hips forward until the front of the hip stretches. Ribs down.

mobility.name: Couch stretch
mobility.how: Back knee on a cushion against a wall, shin up the wall, front foot forward. Tall chest, squeeze the glute.

mobility.name: Hip 90/90 switches
mobility.how: Sit with both knees bent at 90 degrees to one side. Rotate both knees to the other side without using your hands, sitting tall.

mobility.name: Pigeon stretch
mobility.how: From all fours, bring one knee forward behind the wrist, back leg long. Fold forward over the front shin.

mobility.name: Figure-4 glute stretch, lying
mobility.how: On your back, ankle over the other knee, pull that thigh towards you.

mobility.name: Ankle rocks (knee to wall)
mobility.how: Foot 5 to 10 cm from a wall, push the knee forward to touch the wall with the heel down. Move the foot back as you improve.

mobility.name: Standing calf stretch on a wall
mobility.how: Hands on a wall, one leg back straight with the heel down; then bend that knee a little for the lower calf.

mobility.name: Lying hamstring stretch with a towel
mobility.how: On your back, towel round one foot, straight leg up until you feel the back of the thigh. Other leg flat.

mobility.name: Thoracic open book
mobility.how: Lie on your side, knees bent, arms forward together. Open the top arm across to the other side, following it with your eyes.

mobility.name: Cat-cow
mobility.how: On all fours: round the back up slowly, then let the belly drop and lift the chest. Move with the breath.

mobility.name: Towel shoulder pass-through
mobility.how: Hold a towel wide with straight arms, take it over your head and down behind you, then back.

mobility.name: Sleeper stretch (lying on your side)
mobility.how: Lie on one side, upper arm out at 90 degrees, elbow bent. Gently press the forearm down towards the floor with the other hand.

mobility.name: Doorway chest stretch
mobility.how: Forearm on a door frame at shoulder height, step through until the chest stretches.

mobility.name: Deep squat hold
mobility.how: Sit in your deepest squat with heels down, elbows pushing the knees out. Hold a door frame if needed.

mobility.name: Knees-to-chest rock
mobility.how: On your back, hug both knees and rock gently side to side.

mobility.name: Supine spinal twist
mobility.how: On your back, drop both knees to one side, arms out, look the other way.

pelvic.intro: The pelvic floor is the sling of muscle under your pelvis that controls urine, wind and erections, and stabilises the core. Like any muscle it gets stronger with training, and it also has to relax fully. Being able to relax it matters as much as squeezing it.
find: Lie on your back with your knees bent and breathe normally.
Imagine stopping the flow of urine and holding in wind at the same time: draw the area between your legs up and in. The base of the penis pulls in slightly and the testicles lift a little.
Glutes, thighs and belly stay soft. You should be able to keep breathing and talking.
Do not practise by stopping your urine on the toilet: it can stop the bladder emptying properly. Use it once only to find the muscle if you are unsure.
drills: Squeeze and lift for 5 s (build to 10 s), then relax completely for at least as long (5 to 10 s).
Quick strong squeeze for 1 s, full relax for 2 s.
Breathe in slowly through the nose and let the pelvic floor drop and widen, as if letting the belly fill down to the pelvis.
Breathe in: belly, ribs and pelvic floor relax. Breathe out through pursed lips: gently lift the pelvic floor. Never hold your breath while squeezing.
Light lift just before and during the hard part of a movement (standing up from a squat, a bridge, a carry), relax at the top.
levels: 2 x 8 slow (5 s hold, 5 to 10 s relax) + 1 x 10 short, then 6 relaxation breaths, once or twice a day.
Move on when you can do every rep with full relaxation and no breath holding.
2 x 10 slow (8 to 10 s hold, 10 s relax) + 2 x 10 short in sitting and standing.
Move on when the holds feel steady and the relax is complete.
The kegel finisher after strength sessions: lifts during bridges, squats, lunges and carries, with relaxation breaths at the end.
Keep this for maintenance. More is not better.
rules: Relax completely between every contraction. Never hold the pelvic floor tight all day.
Two short practice sessions a day is enough. Overtraining causes tension, pain and urgency.
Stop and see a doctor or pelvic-floor physiotherapist if you get pelvic, testicular or back pain, pain when urinating, or new leaking.
Kegels improve control, continence and pelvic-floor strength. There is no good evidence that they raise testosterone, so the app makes no such claim.

running.detail: The long run grows by at most 1 to 1.5 km a week, total running by about 10% a week, and every 4th week is easier. Most running injuries come from doing too much too soon.
About 80% of your running is at conversation pace. Walk breaks are allowed and planned.

running.rule: Never two hard days in a row
running.detail: Intervals, long runs and leg strength are spread out so the same tissues get 48 h to recover.
Land with the foot under your hips, knee slightly bent, quiet feet. Taking about 5% more steps a minute than feels natural lowers the load on the knee. Do not overstride.
Avoid steep downhills (they load the kneecap hard), uneven or very cambered roads and broken paths. Run on the flattest part of the road.
Cushioned running shoes that fit, replaced every 600 to 800 km. Never race in new shoes; wear them on 2 to 3 runs first.
The 8-minute warm-up before every run and the 5-minute stretch afterwards are part of the session, not extras.
Three strength sessions a week, with glute, hip, quad, hamstring and calf work, are your main injury insurance.
Run before 06:30, drink with a pinch of salt, and go by effort, not pace. Dehydration makes muscles cramp and form fall apart.
Under 6 hours of sleep, or a resting heart rate 7+ bpm above normal, means an easy day instead of a hard one.
Pain 0 to 2 out of 10 that does not grow during the run and is gone the next morning: carry on. 3 or more, or it changes how you run: stop, walk home, and swap the next run for a swim.

swimming.detail: Add no more than about 10% (or 200 m) to your weekly swim distance. The shoulders adapt more slowly than the heart and lungs.
Do the 6-minute pool-deck warm-up every time, and the shoulder-care routine at home on the two harder swim days.

swimming.rule: Hands in front of the shoulders
swimming.detail: Each hand enters the water in line with its shoulder, never across the middle of your head. Crossing over pinches the front of the shoulder.
Breathing every 3 strokes shares the work between both shoulders and keeps the stroke even. Breathing only to one side overloads one shoulder and the neck.
Roll from hip to hip with each stroke. A flat body makes the shoulder do all the work.
Lead the arm forward with a bent, relaxed elbow (fingertip drag). Big straight-arm swings strain the shoulder.
Keep your face down and turn your head with the body to breathe. Lifting the head forward strains the neck and lower back.
While knee care is on: freestyle and backstroke only, no breaststroke kick (its whip kick twists the inside of the knee), and push off the wall gently with both feet.
Kick from the hips with relaxed ankles. Kick on your side rather than with a kickboard if your lower back aches.
Calf or foot cramp in the water: stop at the wall, pull the toes toward you and stretch the calf. Drink well before you swim; you sweat in the pool too.
A pinch at the front or top of the shoulder: switch to kick and backstroke for the rest of the session. If it is there on two swims in a row, see a physiotherapist.
Goggles every time. Tilt the head to drain the ears and dry them after. Shower after the pool.
Open water only with a buddy and a bright tow-float, close to shore, never at dusk. Never swim on the Thursday dry fast.

stop_signs: Swelling, locking or the knee giving way
Pain at night or at rest, or pain that is worse the morning after
Limping, or pain that changes how you run or swim
Pain in the same place on two sessions in a row
Not clearly better after 7 to 10 days of easier training
injury_prevention.stop_action: Any of these: stop that activity and see a physiotherapist or doctor. Keep training what does not hurt (swim if the knee hurts, run or bike if the shoulder hurts).

hyrox.format: Eight rounds of 1 km run + 1 station, in the order above. The clock never stops; transitions are part of your time.

stations.name: SkiErg
stations.home: Jerrycan swings x 20 + 10 burpees per 250 m
stations.cue: Hinge from the hips and drive the handles down past the thighs; arms finish, legs do not squat deep.

stations.name: Sled push
stations.home: Bear crawl 2 x 12 m, or push a loaded backpack on a towel across tiles
stations.cue: Arms straight or slightly bent, low body angle, short powerful steps on the balls of the feet.

stations.name: Sled pull
stations.home: Hand-over-hand towel pull of a loaded jerrycan along the floor, then walk it back
stations.cue: Sit low, lean back, pull the rope hand over hand to the hip and keep the feet still in the box.

stations.name: Burpee broad jumps
stations.home: The same, outside on grass or a clear yard
stations.cue: Chest to the floor, jump forward from both feet, land softly and step into the next one: rhythm beats speed.

stations.name: Rowing
stations.home: Backpack bent-over rows x 30 + squat thrusts x 15 per 250 m
stations.cue: Legs, body, arms on the way back; arms, body, legs on the way forward. Damper about 5 to 6.

stations.name: Farmers carry
stations.home: Two full 20 L jerrycans, walk a loop of the compound
stations.cue: Tall posture, shoulders down, short quick steps. Put them down before your grip fails, not after.

stations.name: Sandbag lunges
stations.home: Backpack walking lunges (rice or sand bags in the backpack)
stations.cue: Back knee touches the floor each step, torso upright, steady breathing: one breath per step.

stations.name: Wall balls
stations.home: Backpack thrusters, or a sand-filled ball thrown at a mark on a strong wall
stations.cue: Full squat, drive up and release at the top in one movement. Break into sets of 10 to 15 from the start.

skills.how: Compromised runs: 1 km straight after a station, at an even effort. The first 200 m always feels worst.
Farmer carries, towel-pull holds and dead hangs (a strong door frame or tree branch if safe). Chalk or a dry towel helps.
Squat depth, catch high, use the legs. Plan the breaks before the start: for example 25, 25, 20, 15, 15.
Step back instead of jumping when tired, keep the broad jump short and consistent, breathe on every landing.
Walk into each station with a plan, start straight away, and run out of the station: practise the change in every simulation.
Heavy bear crawls, backpack pushes on tiles and hill walks with the backpack until you can reach a gym with a sled.

hyrox.gym_note: From the HYROX block (6 to 7 weeks out), try to visit a gym with a SkiErg, rower and sled once a week. Every session also has a home version.

Two full bottles; fuel for rides over 75 min
weekly: Check the tyres for cuts and glass
monthly: Professional service every 3 months or before the 70.3
