smoothies.name: Banana oats and peanut
smoothies.when: Before a long session if you have 90 min to digest, or after strength
smoothies.why: Easy carbs plus some protein and fat. Not low-calorie.
smoothies.how: Blend with 150 ml water and ice. Thick: add more water.

smoothies.name: Avocado banana soy
smoothies.when: Rest days or a light dinner partner
smoothies.why: Healthy fats and potassium. High in calories: keep the avocado to half.
smoothies.how: Unsweetened soy milk. Blend 45 s with ice.

smoothies.name: Mango passion protein
smoothies.when: After a hot session (it is not a low-sugar drink)
smoothies.why: Carbs to refuel plus mtindi protein.
smoothies.how: Sieve the passion seeds if you prefer.

smoothies.name: Banana cocoa groundnut
smoothies.when: After a long run or HYROX session
smoothies.why: Carbs and protein; cocoa for taste and magnesium.
smoothies.how: Unsweetened cocoa only. Blend the karanga first.

smoothies.name: Pineapple ginger soy
smoothies.why: Light and refreshing, still contains natural sugar.

smoothies.name: Long-run refuel
smoothies.when: Sat after the long run or brick (15:00)
smoothies.why: Carbs + protein to refill after the longest session
smoothies.how: Blend the oats dry first, add everything, 45 s. Pinch of salt in the heat.

smoothies.name: Mtindi-embe recovery
smoothies.when: Mon 16:00, between the morning strength session and the evening swim
smoothies.why: Protein from mtindi, slow carbs from oats, omega-3 fats from chia
smoothies.how: Soak chia in the mtindi 5 min, then blend. Swap embe for papai when mango is out of season.

smoothies.name: Beet booster
smoothies.when: Fri 16:00, after the morning strength session
smoothies.why: Beetroot nitrate supports blood flow and endurance (best 2 to 3 h before effort)
smoothies.how: Peel and chop raw beetroot small; blend 60 s. It colours everything red; that is normal.

smoothies.name: Green focus
smoothies.why: Light, high fibre, keeps you full on fewer calories
smoothies.how: Raw sukuma, stems removed. Blend greens with the mtindi first, then the fruit.

smoothies.name: Cocoa-nut strength
smoothies.when: Swap it in for the Mtindi-embe recovery any week
smoothies.why: Healthy fats from nuts, magnesium from cocoa
smoothies.how: Unsweetened cocoa only (not drinking chocolate). Blend 45 s.

smoothies.name: Tikiti hydrator
smoothies.when: Swap-in on very hot days after a long session
smoothies.why: Fluid, potassium and a little salt to replace sweat
smoothies.how: Add a pinch of salt and ice. Drink slowly.

rules.detail: Half the plate vegetables (mchicha, sukuma, kabichi, kachumbari), a quarter protein (palm-size or bigger), a quarter starch (fist-size wali, ugali, ndizi or viazi vitamu).
40 to 60 g protein per meal: e.g. 200 g kuku, 250 g samaki, 3 mayai + 1 cup maharage, or 50 g dagaa + 1 cup dengu.
Your window is 13:00 to 20:00. Water, black coffee or chai without sugar in the morning. Saturday: brunch at 10:30 after the long session.
No soda, juice boxes, energy drinks or sugared chai. Fresh juice counts as sugar: eat the fruit instead. Water 3 to 4 L a day.
Measure: 1 tsp (5 g) per person per dish. Most extra calories in Tanzanian home cooking come from oil.
Chips mayai, maandazi, sambusa, vitumbua and chips: once a week at most, and count them.
Mishkaki (no chips), grilled samaki, ndizi choma, mahindi choma, fruit from the market, supu ya pweza or kuku (go easy on the fat on top).
Weigh them for the first 2 weeks so your eye learns what 150 g looks like. Seconds are where the deficit disappears.
Zero for the cut to 1 Jan. After that, at most 2 drinks a week, never the night before a key session.
Eat protein and vegetables first, one small starch, no second plate. Weddings and sendoffs: plan them into the week.
Use a kitchen scale for the first 2 weeks. After that, use the portion notes in the Foods sheet.
Boil maharage and dengu, 10 eggs, cook dagaa, chop kachumbari. Plans fail on busy weekdays when nothing is ready.

swaps.have: Chai with milk, no sugar, cinnamon or tangawizi for flavour
Water with lime and ice, or sparkling water
20 g measured karanga, korosho, lozi or walnuts

sports.detail: Morning runs on an empty stomach are fine up to 60 min easy. For longer or hard sessions eat 30 to 60 g carbs 60 to 90 min before (a banana and 2 dates), or the evening meal does the job.
Your next meal is the recovery meal: 40 to 60 g protein plus a fist or two of starch within about 2 h. On a two-session day, the smoothie (if it is a smoothie day) or mtindi bridges the gap.
Two or three meals of 40 to 60 g protein each (no breakfast). On fasting days get 120 g or more in the two evening meals.
More starch on the day of and the day after long or hard sessions; less on rest and fasting days. The calorie target already moves with training.
Over 75 min: 30 to 45 g carbs per hour (2 dates = about 36 g), water every 20 min, salt or ORS.
From the first hour: 30 g/h, rising to 60 g/h by June and practising 60 to 90 g/h in July. Mix of drink and food: ndizi, dates, homemade drink.
Familiar breakfast 2 to 3 h before; nothing new on race day; the exact products you practised. Never dry-fast on a race day.
Dar sweat rates are high: 300 to 800 mg sodium per hour in long sessions. ORS sachets or a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lime.
3 to 4 L a day on training days; urine pale yellow. After a dry fast, drink 500 ml to 1 L slowly before eating a big meal.

fuel_progression.when: Nov to Feb (long runs over 75 min)
Jul to Aug (rides 2.5 to 3.5 h, race rehearsal)

hormone.detail: Long, deep deficits and under-fuelling lower testosterone. After 1 Jan the deficit is small, and training days get more carbs.
At least 0.8 g fat per kg a day (about 65 g): avocado, karanga, ufuta, eggs, fish.
About 160 g a day spread over your meals.
Progressive strength training three times a week.
7 to 9 hours; poor sleep is one of the fastest ways to lower testosterone.
Easy weeks, rest days and not stacking hard sessions.
Very high endurance volume with too little food suppresses hormones: the plan raises volume gradually and fuels long sessions.

hormone.topic: What the app will not do
hormone.detail: No testosterone boosters, no hormone products. Foods, kegels and supplements do not guarantee higher testosterone. If you have symptoms, see a doctor for a blood test.

nutrition.smoothie_rule: At most one smoothie a day, and not every day. Fruit smoothies are not automatically low-calorie or low-sugar: they count as a meal or a snack.

supplements.name: Creatine monohydrate
supplements.purpose: More strength and repeat power, better recovery between hard sets.
supplements.dose: 3 to 5 g a day (studied range; no loading needed)
supplements.when: Any time, daily; in water or the smoothie
supplements.side_effects: Water weight of 1 to 2 kg in the first weeks; stomach upset if taken in big doses at once
supplements.cautions: Kidney disease or kidney medicines: ask a doctor first. Drink 3+ L of water a day.

supplements.name: Omega-3 (EPA + DHA)
supplements.purpose: Heart health, joints, may help recovery.
supplements.dose: 1 to 2 g EPA + DHA a day
supplements.cautions: Blood thinners or a bleeding disorder: ask a doctor. Oily fish (dagaa, sardini) days can replace it.

supplements.name: Vitamin D3
supplements.purpose: Bone, muscle and immune health when you are low.
supplements.dose: 1,000 to 2,000 IU a day; do not exceed 4,000 IU without a doctor
supplements.side_effects: Very rare at these doses; too much raises blood calcium
supplements.cautions: Best: test 25-OH vitamin D first. Kidney stones or high calcium: doctor first.

supplements.name: Vitamin K2 (MK-7)
supplements.purpose: Often paired with vitamin D for calcium handling in bones.
supplements.cautions: Do NOT take with warfarin or other vitamin K antagonist blood thinners.

supplements.name: Magnesium (glycinate)
supplements.purpose: Sleep quality, cramps; you lose some in sweat.
supplements.side_effects: Loose stools (more with citrate or oxide forms)
supplements.cautions: Kidney disease: ask a doctor first.

supplements.name: Zinc
supplements.purpose: Immune function; only helps if your diet is low.
supplements.dose: 8 to 15 mg (upper limit 40 mg a day from all sources)
supplements.side_effects: Nausea on an empty stomach; long-term high doses lower copper
supplements.cautions: Dagaa, maini, nyama and seeds already supply it. Not a testosterone booster.

supplements.name: Electrolytes / ORS
supplements.purpose: Prevents cramping, headaches and the late-session fade in the heat.
supplements.dose: About 300 to 800 mg sodium per hour of sweaty exercise; 1 ORS sachet per 500 ml to 1 L
supplements.when: Sessions over 60 min, long hot days, after breaking a dry fast if you trained the day before
supplements.cautions: High blood pressure or heart or kidney disease: ask a doctor about sodium.

supplements.name: Protein powder (non-whey)
supplements.purpose: Convenience when food protein falls short.
supplements.evidence: Strong for total protein, not better than food
supplements.when: After training if a meal is more than 2 h away
supplements.cautions: You chose no whey. Food covers your target, so it is not in your plan; a plant protein is an option if you ever need it.

supplements.name: Caffeine (kahawa / chai)
supplements.purpose: Better effort in intervals and races.
supplements.dose: 1 to 3 mg per kg (about 100 to 200 mg, 1 to 2 cups coffee)
supplements.when: 45 min before hard sessions; nothing after 12:00
supplements.cautions: High blood pressure, anxiety or palpitations: keep it low.

supplements_note: Ranges are the doses studied in research, not prescriptions. Start low, one new supplement at a time, and check with a doctor or pharmacist if you take any medicine or have a medical condition. Not in the plan: protein powder (your protein comes from mayai, dagaa, samaki, kuku, maharage and mtindi), fat burners, and "testosterone booster" blends. They add cost without reliable benefit.

sleep.what: Wake at the same time every day, weekends included
sleep.why: A fixed wake time is the strongest anchor for your body clock.

sleep.what: Toilet, weigh, glass of water with a pinch of salt
sleep.why: Same conditions every morning makes the weight trend honest.

sleep.what: Outdoor light 5 to 10 min (the morning run counts)
sleep.why: Morning daylight sets your sleep timer for tonight. No sunglasses for this.
After 12:00 caffeine is still in your blood at 22:00.
Last big meal at least 2 h before bed so digestion does not disturb sleep.
On two-session days. Longer naps make night sleep worse.
Bright overhead light and phone glare delay melatonin.
A cool shower helps your core temperature drop, which triggers sleep.

sleep.what: Phone on charge outside the bedroom; 5 min physiological sighs (two inhales through the nose, one long exhale)
Lights out. Target 7.5 h asleep, 8 h in bed
sleep.why: Sleep is when fat loss, muscle repair and hormone balance happen.

bedroom.what: Fan on and aimed at you, window open with a mosquito net or screens. Ideal room around 24 to 26 C if you have AC.
Blackout curtain or a cheap eye mask. Cover standby lights with tape.
Foam ear plugs for dogs, bajaji, music or the mosque/church loudspeaker at dawn.
Treated mosquito net every night. Malaria costs 1 to 3 weeks of training.
No work or scrolling in bed. If awake 20 min, get up, read in dim light, return when sleepy.

recovery.how: Every 4th build week is easier (fewer sets, shorter long run), plus taper weeks before races and recovery weeks after them. Do not add extra work.
Easy runs at talking pace. Most fitness gains come from easy volume plus a few hard sessions.
10 to 20 min lying down with a guided recording (search "NSDR" on YouTube).
Recovery-day routine (20 min) and the 7-min morning routine.
Log sleep, soreness, energy, stress and resting heart rate on Home. The coach changes today's plan only when several signs agree, never from one number.
Fever, malaria symptoms or chest infection: stop training, see a doctor, return gradually. Never train through a fever.
Joint or tendon pain that gets worse during a run: stop, swim or bike instead for 3 days. Pain for 2 weeks: see a physiotherapist.

tanzania.meaning: Dar es Salaam sits around 26 to 33 C with high humidity. Sweat evaporates poorly and heart rate climbs.
tanzania.todo: Runs before 07:00 (start 05:45 to 06:15). PM sessions after 17:30, indoors or in shade. Never 11:00 to 16:00.

tanzania.meaning: Expect to run 30 to 60 s per km slower than cool-weather charts at the same effort.
tanzania.todo: Train by effort (RPE) and the talk test, not pace.

tanzania.meaning: You can lose 1 to 1.5 L of sweat an hour.
tanzania.todo: 3 to 4 L water a day; ORS or salt for sessions over 60 min; weigh before and after a long run to learn your sweat rate.

tanzania.meaning: November to December, during the 10 km build.
tanzania.todo: Indoor fallback for every session: the home strength and Hyrox work needs only a room.

tanzania.meaning: Roughly March to May, right when cycling starts.
tanzania.todo: Have a spin bike option (gym class) for rainy days. Avoid riding on flooded or slippery roads.

tanzania.meaning: Open water is calmest early morning; currents and boats are the danger.
tanzania.todo: Swim with a buddy, near the shore, with a bright tow-float. Never alone, never at dusk.

tanzania.meaning: Hotel, club and gym pools: many sell monthly passes. Closures happen.
tanzania.todo: Have a second pool option. If both are shut, do a Hyrox HIIT or strength session instead.

tanzania.meaning: Traffic with daladala, bodaboda and trucks.
tanzania.todo: Ride early (06:00 to 07:30) on quieter roads, helmet always, front and rear lights, bright top, mirror. Or ride a spin bike.
A second-hand road bike in good condition is enough for a first 70.3. Get it serviced and professionally fitted; buy a helmet, lights, two bottle cages and a puncture kit.

tanzania.meaning: As far as I know there is no Hyrox event in Tanzania.
tanzania.todo: Check hyrox.com for the nearest June race and set its real date in Profile > Races. If travel does not work, do the full simulation at a gym on the day and count it.

tanzania.meaning: There is no Ironman 70.3 in Tanzania as far as I know; the nearest are abroad.
tanzania.todo: Choose the August 70.3 early, book travel, and set its date in Profile > Races. For the July Olympic tune-up ask clubs in Dar es Salaam or Zanzibar, or do a timed simulation.

tanzania.meaning: Home substitutes work, but real machines help in February.
tanzania.todo: From January, 1 or 2 gym visits a week for the SkiErg, rower and sled if a gym near you has them.
Treated net every night, repellent at dawn and dusk runs. Test early if feverish.

tanzania.meaning: You are starting at about 87.5 kg at 162 cm and training up to twice a day.
tanzania.todo: A quick check-up (blood pressure, blood sugar, and vitamin D if possible) before week 3 is a good idea.

injury.note: A small pinch in the knee joint during the 8 km run in Dodoma on 14 Nov.
advice: A small pinch that stays at 0 to 2 out of 10 and settles within a day is usually an overload sign after a jump in distance, not damage.
Until it settles: flat routes, no sprints or hills, no deep or loaded knee bends, the long run held at its current distance, and the knee-care routine every day.
Stop a run if the pain reaches 3 out of 10 or changes how you run. Swap the next run for a swim.
See a physiotherapist or doctor if it hurts on two runs in a row, if the knee swells, locks, gives way or hurts at night, or if it is not clearly better in 7 to 10 days.
The app is a coach, not a diagnosis. When in doubt, get it checked before race day.

weekly_rule: ON TRACK: change nothing. BEHIND (7-day average more than 1 kg above the target line): check your logging first (oil, chapati, sugar in chai, weekends), then remove one fist of starch a day for 7 days. TOO FAST (more than 1.5 kg below): add 150 kcal a day. Adherence under 80%: fix consistency before changing anything else.
